newsitem.title: CHINA: China B stocks recover, A shares end mixed.
newsitem.headline: China B stocks recover, A shares end mixed.

text.p: China's foreign currency B shares recovered on Monday with investors putting behind them the sharp falls of last week, while domestic A shares closed mixed, brokers said.
The Shenzhen B share index rallied 7.68 points, or 6.11 percent, to close at 133.24. Volume was 44.69 million shares worth HK$194.31 million (US$24.9 million) against Friday's HK$191.59 million.
Brokers said the rise was fuelled by institutional demand for shares of firms expected to post strong earnings this year.
The average P/E ratio of Shenzhen-listed B shares is now below 20, which discouraged selling, brokers said.

"Selling pressure eased on Monday after declines in the past few sessions, and buying focused on blue-chip counters ahead of the corporate reporting season," a broker with a major Chinese brokerage said.
In Shanghai, the B share index rose 0.944 points, or 1.48 percent, to 64.678 points. Volume was 17.2 million shares worth $8.1 million.
The Shanghai B index lost 3.84 percent last week on volatile trading after Beijing launched a crackdown on the stock markets.
Brokers said sentiment had stabilised with the shock of the crackdown nearly over and trading was slow as overseas investors left the market ahead of the Christmas holiday.
"With market fundamentals improving, most investors did not want to sell their shares at current low prices, and long-term investors started building positions," one broker said.
"The index is likely to rise above the 65-point resistance level tomorrow, which would trigger follow-up buying," a second broker said.
Shanghai A shares rose on a technical rebound after sharp falls in the past week, but market sentiment remained cautious with limited follow-up buying after last week's crackdown, brokers said.
The A index closed up 17.606 points, or 1.91 percent, to 939.946 points. Volume was 404.0 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan ($422 million).

In Shenzhen, the A share market maintained its downward trend with continued selling of cheap and small shares and market sentiment still overshadowed by Beijing's stock crackdown last week, brokers said.
The A index declined 6.71 points, or 2.04 percent, to end at 322.25, with turnover rising to 5.12 billion yuan from 4.27 billion yuan on Friday.
